description.shortText: Robots powered by machine learning and machine vision, designed to monitor and assist the elderly and people with disabilities in performing daily tasks.

attachments.name: Would You Let a Robot Take Care of Your Mother?
attachments.description: Robotic companions are being promoted as an antidote to the burden of longer, lonelier human lives. At stake is the future of what it means to be human.

attachments.name: How Robot Caregivers Will Help an Aging U.S. Population
attachments.description: Robots are being used to keep age 65-plus people healthy and alert. Learn more on how robot caregivers will help fill the upcoming caregiving void in the U.S.

attachments.name: ROBOTS could soon keep the elderly company
attachments.description: The three-year project to create a 'culturally-aware' robot will be led by teams from Middlesex University and the University of Bedfordshire.

attachments.name: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Elderly Care Robotics
attachments.description: In this article, we look at prevalence of artificial intelligence being deployed in elder care robots currently and what is in store for the the future

attachments.name: Could a robot care for grandma?
attachments.description: In the future, machines could be programmed to assist and comfort the elderly—and help meet the escalating demand for caregivers.

attachments.name: Can Robots Ease the Caregiver Burden?
attachments.description: A small robot army is being test-driven in long-term care facilities throughout Toronto to fill an urgent need—to look after our elderly. But what is lost when we outsource caregiving to machines?

attachments.name: Pepper Robots for Enhanced Elderly Health
attachments.description: The rise in the elderly population these decades has paved the way for innovations catering to elderly health care. One of them, Pepper Robots, is on point.

attachments.name: AI Could Provide Moment-by-Moment Nursing for a Hospital’s Sickest Patients.
attachments.description: In the intensive care unit, artificial intelligence can keep watch at a patient’s bedside

attachments.name: Meet Zora, the Robot Caregiver
attachments.description: This robot is at the center of an experiment in France to change care for elderly patients.

attachments.name: Robot caregivers: harbingers of expanded freedom for all?
attachments.description: As we near a time when robots may serve a vital function by becoming caregivers, it is important to examine the ethical implications of this development. By applying the capabilities approach as a guide to both the design and use of robot caregivers, we hope that this will maximize opportunities to preserve or expand freedom for care recipients. We think the use of the capabilities approach will be especially valuable for improving the ability of impaired persons to interface more effectively with their physical and social environments.

attachments.name: Elder Care Robots Are Necessary and Imminent, Say European Experts
attachments.description: Lilly is very dear to Mrs. Rosenberg, but not someone she would meet for a glass of wine. Lilly is a so-called welfare or elder care robot, and the likes of her are on their way into our homes, as healthcare providers around the world are under pressure to deliver services to a growing population of elderly people.

attachments.name: The Future of Robot Caregivers.
attachments.description: Elderly people need everyday help, and there aren’t enough humans to provide it.
